column5: An agent loop: the context goes to a stateless LLM call, tool calls are run by the harness and appended to the transcript, and the loop ends on a final answer or a harness limit.
Agent memory as a write path that extracts facts into a long-term store, a read path that retrieves them back into context, and consolidation that merges or expires stored facts.

Plan-and-Execute: a planner writes an inspectable step list, an executor runs the current step, an on-track check moves to the next step, sends surprises to a replanner that rewrites the rest, or returns the answer; ReWOO and LLMCompiler shown as variants.

A function-calling sequence: your code sends messages and tool schemas, the model returns a get_weather tool call, your code validates and executes it, sends the result back by call ID, and the model writes the final reply.

MCP architecture: a host app runs one MCP client per server, talking JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdio to a local server and over Streamable HTTP to a remote one, with a comparison showing M times N integrations becoming M plus N.

A parent agent briefs a read-only subagent to find callers of an auth API and a shell subagent to summarize failing tests; each fills its own fresh context window and returns only a short result, so the parent context grows by two small entries.

Context compaction as three context-window bars: near the 70 to 95 percent trigger, after old tool results are cleared to stubs, and, if still over, rebuilt as system prompt plus summary plus the last N turns, beside what the summary must keep.

A support-ticket graph: an LLM classifies the ticket, code routes it to billing, tech or human review, a grounded check sends the reply on pass, retries the tech node once on failure and escalates to a human after two failures, with typed state and a checkpoint after each node.

Privilege separation against indirect prompt injection: a planner LLM with tools sees only the trusted request and writes a plan as code, a quarantined LLM without tools reads untrusted content and returns tainted typed values, and an interpreter with taint-tracking policy allows tool calls or blocks and asks a human when tainted data reaches a sensitive sink.

A human-in-the-loop sequence: the agent calls issue_refund for 480 USD, harness policy requires approval over 200, checkpoints state, asks the human with exact parameters, the human edits it to 300 USD, and the agent resumes with the decision as the tool result, beside a risk scale from reversible and small to irreversible and large.

The reflection loop: generate, verify with tests, a validator or a critic, return on pass, or on failure reflect on what to change and store the lesson in memory for the next attempt, with Self-Refine, Reflexion and evaluator-optimizer as variants and a note that self-correction without an external signal often fails.

A support-agent graph: verify identity, triage by intent, risk and sentiment, escalate high-risk requests or requests for a human, otherwise let a scoped agent act with human approval over a limit, reply when a grounded check passes, and escalate with a structured handoff after two failures or no progress.

Sakana Fugu: one query goes to a learned orchestrator that either scores the pool models with a selection head and routes to one worker (fast) or writes a per-query workflow whose workers are combined (Ultra), both drawing on a pool of frontier, open and specialized models.

A computer-use loop: the harness sends the task, recent screenshots and history to a multimodal model, which returns a click at coordinates; the harness scales and performs it on a sandboxed VM and captures a new screenshot, keeping only the last few screenshots and turning older steps into text notes.

A decision ladder that defaults to code: writable rules mean code, tabular input means classical ML, intolerable errors mean a human decides with AI assisting, value below cost means code, and only otherwise an LLM component with evals, beside a note that most solutions are a hybrid of code and one model step.

A RAG error-analysis tree over the pipeline stages: if the answer is not in the corpus it is a content gap, if the right chunk is not in the top 50 fix retrieval, if it is not in the final top-k add or tune a reranker, otherwise fix generation, with recall@k at 5, 20 and 50 on labelled failures as the number that splits retrieval from generation.
